subject: HelixMed — LLM API porting: discovery recap & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tully <sam.tully@helixmed.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helixmed.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: HelixMed discovery — porting off proprietary LLM APIs (recap)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have aligned next steps and success criteria before we draft an SOW / PoC plan. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described
- Cost predictability: current spend on OpenAI/Anthropic spikes with batch inference and multi-model experiments.
- Vendor lock & long-term risk: concern about API changes and model availability for clinical workloads.
- Latency: chat + context-heavy prompts occasionally breach 500ms tail SLO for triage workflows.
- Data governance: need for VPC/on-prem options and support for customer-managed KMS for PHI.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Front-end + request routing: in-house microservices (Node.js) calling OpenAI (chat/completions) and Anthropic for policy/assistant variants.
- Embeddings: currently using OpenAI embeddings for vector search (Pinecone).
- Model orchestration: homegrown router that toggles between models based on prompt type.
- Monitoring: basic request logs + Datadog; no token-level cost attribution today.

Success criteria for a successful port
- Compatibility: parity with function-calling, streaming responses, and existing JSON-structured outputs.
- Cost: target >=35% reduction in per-token cost for batch evals; predictable committed throughput for peak hours.
- Latency: P95 inference < 350ms on primary routes (triage) for 2k concurrent users.
- Security & compliance: private deployment option (VPC) with KMS support and SOC2 evidence.
- Quality: model output quality comparable to current top-choice (Anthropic) on your safety/accuracy eval set.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial)
- Llama 3 (quantized, Redwood-verified profile) — strong for chat + function calling.
- Mistral Instruct family — cost-effective candidate for generative tasks.
- Falcon-40B Instruct — strong for long-context instruction-following.

Compatibility concerns to validate in PoC
- End-to-end function calling semantics and structured JSON outputs.
- Tokenization differences impacting prompt engineering and safety classifiers.
- Embeddings API parity (dimensions, deterministic options) for vector store reindexing.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood provides a 4-week PoC: onboarding, runbook, and two target routes (chat triage + embeddings).
2) HelixMed provides a redacted eval set (5–10 representative prompts + expected outputs) and access to non-production credentials for integrated testing.
3) Security pre-check: exchange SOC2 artifacts and start the Private deployment questionnaire.
4) Deliverable after PoC: cost/latency report, regression matrix vs Anthropic/OpenAI, and SOW for production migration.

Attachments we referenced: HelixMed_RFP.pdf attached for reference.

Timeline: propose kickoff on Mon 2026-03-30 if approvals are in place.

Thanks again — I’ll draft SOW outline and circulate by EOD Friday.

—
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sam Tully <sam.tully@helixmed.ai>

Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@helixmed.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelixMed discovery — porting off proprietary LLM APIs (recap)

Aditya —

Appreciate the thorough recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- The 500ms breaches are most common for the triage route when the context includes the full patient interaction (12–18 turns).
- For embeddings, consistency matters more than exact dimensionality — we can reindex but want to avoid long reindex windows.
- Security: we need HSM-backed KMS for production; VPC is required.

We can share a redacted eval set by next Wednesday (2026-03-25). Kickoff on 3/30 looks fine for our PM and infra lead.

One ask: can you include a quick note in the SOW about rollback/fallback to Anthropic in case of quality regression during rollout? That would be important for our compliance review.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of Data Products
HelixMed
